Parthia: Historical region located in northeastern Iran. Parthia (Old Persian: 𐎱𐎼𐎰𐎺 Parθava; Parthian: 𐭐𐭓𐭕𐭅 Parθaw; Middle Persian: 𐭯𐭫𐭮𐭥𐭡𐭥 Pahlaw) is a historical region located in northeastern Greater Iran.

Its name comes from Ancient Greek for "love of wisdom," and once upon a time physics and psychology were considered branches of it before going their separate academic ways. What rational, critical field is this?
Philosophy: Study of general and fundamental questions.
Often depicted as a beautiful woman with butterfly wings, this mortal-turned-immortal endured trials set by Venus to win back her husband Cupid in Apuleius's The Golden Ass — who is she?
Psyche (mythology): Wife of Cupid. Psyche is known from the ancient Roman proto-novel The Golden Ass (also known as the Metamorphoses), written by philosopher and orator Apuleius in the 2nd century.
This crusader lord ruled Antioch and Transjordan by right of marriage, and once tortured the Latin Patriarch of Antioch over unpaid funds before raiding Byzantine Cyprus — who was he?
Raynald of Châtillon: Crusader and military leader (1125–1187)
The longest-serving U.S. secretary of defense, this Cold War-era Pentagon chief championed systems analysis and escalated American involvement in the Vietnam War — who was he?
Robert McNamara: American businessman and government official (1916–2009)
This politician resigned as Kyrgyzstan's acting president in November 2020 just so he could run in — and win — the 2021 election that made him the country's sixth president. Who is he?
Sadyr Japarov: President of Kyrgyzstan since 2021. Japarov returned to Kyrgyzstan in 2017, where he was arrested and sentenced to an 11 year prison term due to his prior illegal political activities.

This early 20th-century youth movement emphasizes outdoor skills like camping and woodcraft, uses a uniform designed to hide social class differences, and awards merit badges bearing a fleur-de-lis. What movement is it?
Scouting: Youth movement. Scouting or the Scout Movement is a youth movement which became popularly established in the first decade of the 20th century.
One of Noah's sons in Genesis, this biblical figure is considered an ancestor of Abraham and lent his name to the term for a group of West Asian peoples — who is he?
Shem: Biblical figure, son of Noah. Shem (Hebrew: שֵׁם Šēm; Arabic: سَام, romanized: Sām) is one of the sons of Noah in the Bible (Genesis 5–11 and 1 Chronicles 1:4).
This left-wing ideology is defined by social ownership of the means of production — public, cooperative, or employee-held — rather than private ownership. What is it?
Socialism: Political philosophy emphasising social ownership of production.
Nicknamed the 'Tiger King' for his ferocity, this 29th monarch of the Ayutthaya Kingdom is credited with devising the fundamental techniques of Muay Thai — who is he?
Known by a name meaning 'behind the pool' after the palace where he resided, this monarch ruled the Ayutthaya Kingdom from 1709 to 1733 as the third ruler of the Ban Phlu Luang dynasty — who is he?
Thai Sa: King of Ayutthaya. The name "Thai Sa" (lit. "behind the pool") refers to the Banyongrattanat Palace, which was located by a pool where he often resided.

Japan's first socialist premier in nearly half a century, this 1990s prime minister is best remembered for an official statement apologizing for his country's past colonial wars on the 50th anniversary of WWII's end. Who was he?
Tomiichi Murayama: Prime Minister of Japan from 1994 to 1996.
This Russian dissident and writer founded and chaired the Democratic Union party and sat on the editorial board of The New Times before her death in 2014 — who is she?
Controlled until 2023 by Yevgeny Prigozhin, this Russian state-funded private military company first emerged fighting in the Donbas war — which group?
Wagner Group: Russian private military company. The Wagner Group has used infrastructure of the Russian Armed Forces.
Dying just 31 days into office in 1841, this ninth U.S. president holds the record for shortest term ever served — who is he?
William Henry Harrison: President of the United States in 1841.
Cairo-born and a founding member of Fatah, he chaired the PLO from 1969 until his death in 2004 — which Palestinian leader?
Yasser Arafat: President of Palestine from 1989 to 2004.
Elected mayor of Guatemala City six times, this president's crowning achievement was the 1996 peace accord that ended his country's 36-year civil war — who was he?
Who among these four was born earliest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these people was born first?
Henrietta Swan Leavitt (born 1868) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
William Osler (born 1849) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these came out first?
TeX (published 1978) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Vikram Sarabhai is a physicist. Often regarded as the "Father of Indian space program", Sarabhai was honored with Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously) in 1972.
Who among these is a chemist?
Glenn T. Seaborg is a chemist. Throughout his career, Seaborg worked for arms control.
What is the atomic number of Beryllium?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
In what year was Henk Rogers born?
Henk Rogers is a Dutch-born American video game designer and entrepreneur.
In what year was Ptolemy born?
Ptolemy: The first was his astronomical treatise now known as the Almagest, originally entitled Mathēmatikḗ Syntaxis (Μαθηματικὴ Σύνταξις, 'Mathematical Treatise').
In what year was Michael Burry born?
Michael Burry: Michael James Burry (born June 19, 1971) is an American investor, hedge fund manager, and licensed physician.
In what year did Frank Oppenheimer die?
Frank Oppenheimer: The younger brother of renowned physicist J.
In what year did Hippocrates die?
Hippocrates is also widely recognized for his contributions to medical ethics, being credited with the Hippocratic Oath that remains in use today.
In what year was Oganesson discovered?
Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
In what year was Arsenic discovered?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
Indometacin: Pfizer. It works by inhibiting the production of prostaglandins, endogenous signaling molecules known to cause these symptoms.
In which country is Blood orange?
Blood orange: Italy. The blood orange is a variety of orange with crimson, near blood-colored flesh.
Who is credited with discovering Iodine?
Iodine: Bernard Courtois. Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
Who is credited with discovering Mendelevium?
Mendelevium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md (formerly Mv) and atomic number 101.
Who is credited with discovering Magnesium?
Magnesium: Joseph Black. Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
This long-term skin condition occurs when dead skin cells and oil clog hair follicles, producing blackheads, whiteheads, and pimples mainly on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne is a long-term skin condition that occurs when dead skin cells and sebum clog hair follicles.
This Indian economist won the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his work on welfare economics and has also studied the causes of famines — who is he?
Amartya Sen (born 3 November 1933) is an Indian economist and philosopher.
The largest genus in the arum family with roughly 1,000 species, this flowering plant group is native to the Americas, ranging from northern Mexico down to northern Argentina — which genus?
Anthurium (Schott, 1829) is a genus of about 1,000 species of flowering plants, the largest genus of the arum family, Araceae.

It's one of the oldest natural sciences, recruiting math, physics, and chemistry to explain everything that originates beyond Earth's atmosphere — from comets and quasars to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
Astronomy is a natural science that studies celestial objects and the phenomena that occur in the cosmos.

This fluid-dynamics rule holds that a fluid's pressure drops as its speed increases; the Swiss physicist credited with it published the idea in 1738, though Leonhard Euler derived the actual equation — what's it called?
Bernoulli's principle is a key concept in fluid dynamics that relates pressure, speed and height.
Caused by a toxin that thrives in low-oxygen conditions — the same one sold cosmetically as 'botox' — this rare illness brings blurred vision and creeping paralysis but rarely a fever. What is it?
Botulism is a rare and potentially fatal illness caused by botulinum toxin (commonly referred to as botox), which is produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum.

The largest land bird in North America went fully extinct in the wild in 1987 when every survivor was captured for breeding — which critically endangered vulture has since returned to the Grand Canyon and beyond?
California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.
This worldwide family of over 5,000 fly species — found everywhere except the Antarctic and Arctic — includes the biting midges also known as sand flies — what is it called?
Ceratopogonidae is a family of flies colloquially known as no-see-ums, sand flies, or biting midges, generally 1-3 millimetres (116-18 in) in length.
An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned what he learned there into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen-food industry. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye (December 9, 1886 - October 7, 1956) was an American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist, who is widely considered the founder of the modern frozen food industry.
Thanks to variations in the OR6A2 gene, some people taste this Mediterranean herb as fresh and citrusy while others swear it tastes like soap — its leaves are called cilantro in the US. What is it?
Coriander is an annual herb in the family Apiaceae.

This American nuclear physicist worked on the Manhattan Project and later led the Federation of American Scientists, best remembered for his 1959 testimony that helped sink a controversial cabinet nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill (November 11, 1919 - December 14, 2008) was an American nuclear physicist who worked on the Manhattan Project during World War II and was head of the Federation of American Scientists.
This waterfowl belongs to the same family as swans and geese, but is generally smaller and shorter-necked — and despite the shared family, swans and geese don't count as one. What is it?
Duck is the common name for numerous species of waterfowl in the family Anatidae.
This Italian-American physicist won the 1938 Nobel Prize, built the world's first artificial nuclear reactor (Chicago Pile-1), and is called the "architect of the nuclear age" — who was he?

Enrico Fermi (29 September 1901 - 28 November 1954) was an Italian-American physicist, renowned for being the creator of the world's first artificial nuclear reactor, the Chicago Pile-1, and a member of the Manhattan Project.
Immature at birth but developed by puberty, this network of organs includes the vagina, uterus, and fallopian tubes, protected by a fold called the labia majora — what's it called?
Female reproductive system is made up of the internal and external sex organs that function in the reproduction of new offspring.

A French economist who gave lectures up and down the country and helped found the Inter-Parliamentary Union, he shared the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901 for his work in Europe's peace movement — who was he?
Frédéric Passy (20 May 1822 - 12 June 1912) was a French economist and pacifist who was a founding member of several peace societies and the Inter-Parliamentary Union.
Caused in over 90% of cases by iodine deficiency, this visible swelling in the neck comes from an enlarged thyroid gland — name the condition?
Goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.

A spiny mammal with 17 species across five genera in Europe, Asia, and Africa, this creature shares distant ancestry with shrews. There are no native populations in Australia or the Americas, though one extinct genus once roamed North America—what is it?
Hedgehog is a spiny mammal of the subfamily Erinaceinae, in the eulipotyphlan family Erinaceidae.
A colourless, ammonia-scented liquid with formula N2H4, this hazardous compound foams polymers, inflates airbags, and serves as a storable spacecraft propellant. What is it?
Hydrazine is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula N2H4.
Lasting anywhere from a few days to over a month, this disorder makes it hard to fall or stay asleep, leaving daytime drowsiness, irritability and trouble focusing in its wake — what is it?
Insomnia is a sleep disorder causing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep for as long as desired.
This American physicist revived general relativity in postwar America and had a knack for naming things — coining "quantum foam," "wormhole," and the term "black hole" itself. Who is he?
John Archibald Wheeler (July 9, 1911 - April 13, 2008) was an American theoretical physicist.

Normally part of the healthy flora in the mouth, skin, and gut, this rod-shaped bacterium can turn destructive if aspirated into the lungs, producing a telltale bloody, brick-colored jelly-like sputum — what's the organism?
Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative, non-motile, encapsulated, lactose-fermenting, facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium.
Viruses muddy its definition, and it might exist beyond Earth in unfamiliar forms — but on this planet it fills air, water and soil, even harsh niches of extremophiles. What is it?
Life is the capacity, in matter, for processes such as cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, cell growth, adaptation, response to stimuli, and reproduction.
This alpha-amino acid, a building block for many proteins, carries a side chain that stays partially charged at the body's normal pH, classifying it among the basic amino acids — what is it?
Lysine (symbol Lys or K) is an -amino acid that is a precursor to many proteins.
A German historian, jurist, and political economist born in 1864, he is counted among the central founders of sociology and still shapes social theory today — who was he?

Max Weber (21 April 1864 - 14 June 1920) was a German sociologist, historian, jurist, and political economist who was one of the central figures in the development of sociology and the social sciences more generally.
Widowed in 2021, this Israeli-American billionaire physician publishes Israel Hayom and has been among the most prominent financial supporters of a US president since 2016 — who is she?
Miriam Adelson (ne Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.
This protective plate at fingertips and toe-tips is found in nearly every primate except marmosets, and is made of the same tough protein found in claws, hooves, and horns — what is it?

Nail (anatomy) is a protective plate characteristically found at the tip of the digits (fingers and toes) of almost all primates (except for marmosets), corresponding to the claws in other tetrapod animals.
Built from nucleotide units of a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogenous base, these biomolecules come in two main classes distinguished by whether their sugar is ribose or deoxyribose — what are they?
Nucleic acid are large biomolecules that are crucial in all cells and viruses.
Belonging to the pea family and native to Mesoamerica, this vine produces blue or white flowers and an edible tuberous root known in Spanish as jícama — which species?
Pachyrhizus erosus (from Nahuatl languages: xicamatl) or Mexican turnip, is a native Mesoamerican vine, although the name jicama most commonly refers to the plant's edible tuberous root.

Nicknamed with the backronym 'Practical Extraction and Reporting Language,' this dynamic scripting language was developed by Larry Wall in 1987 and borrows features from C, AWK, and sed — which language?
Perl is a high-level, general-purpose, interpreted, dynamic programming language.
Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and often spread by flea bites, this disease comes in pneumonic, bubonic, and septicemic forms — what is it?
Plague (disease) is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. There are three forms of plague, each affecting a different part of the body and causing associated symptoms.
Including raccoons, coatis, kinkajous, and ringtails, this New World mammal family within the order Carnivora is made up mostly of omnivores — what family is it?
Procyonidae is a New World family of the order Carnivora. Procyonidae ( PROH-see-ON-i-dee) is a New World family of the order Carnivora.
Decades after leaving the Communist Party of Spain to found the United Left, which economist re-emerged in 2023 as an unlikely no-confidence-vote candidate?
Ramón Tamames (born 1 November 1933) is a Spanish economist and former politician.
This woody perennial flowering plant, genus Rosa in the family Rosaceae, includes over 300 species and tens of thousands of cultivars, with sharp prickles on many stems — name the flower?
Rose is either a woody perennial flowering plant of the genus Rosa, in the family Rosaceae, or the flower it bears.
This synthetic element, atomic number 106, is so fleeting that only a few atoms exist at a time and decay within minutes — and it's named for an American nuclear chemist; what is it?
Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Whether on land, in fresh water, or in the sea, this gastropod earns its name from a coiled shell roomy enough to fully retract into — what is it?
Snail is a shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.

Starting with fever and flu-like symptoms before the skin blisters and peels into painful raw patches, this severe drug-triggered skin reaction sits on the same disease spectrum as toxic epidermal necrolysis, only less severe — which condition?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a type of severe skin reaction.
Defined as applying conceptual knowledge to reach practical goals in a repeatable way, this field covers both tangible machines and intangible things like software — what is it?
Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.
A nightshade-family relative of tobacco and the potato, this South American native arrived in Eurasia via the Columbian exchange and is botanically a berry eaten as a vegetable — what is it?
Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is a plant whose fruit is an edible berry that is eaten as a vegetable.
This medical condition involves involuntary muscle spasms that interfere with vaginal intercourse or other penetration, often causing pain from the first attempt — what is it?
Vaginismus is a condition in which involuntary muscle spasm interferes with vaginal intercourse or other penetration of the vagina.
A physician and Royal Society charter member, he surveyed confiscated Irish land for Cromwell's soldiers but is best remembered for pioneering 'political arithmetic' in economics — who was he?
William Petty (26 May 1623 - 16 December 1687) was an English economist, physician, scientist and philosopher.
The first Muslim scientist to win a Nobel Prize, this Pakistani theoretical physicist shared the 1979 Physics prize for unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces — who was he?
First flown in October 1972, this was the world's first twin-engine wide-body airliner, born from a 1967 France-West Germany-UK collaboration that later lost its British partner — what is it?
Airbus A300: World's first twin-engine widebody jet airliner.
This three-star system includes Proxima, the closest star to the Sun, and shines as the third-brightest point in the night sky after Sirius and Canopus — which system?
Alpha Centauri: Star system in the Centaurus constellation.
Commonly called windflowers, which genus of the buttercup family is native to every continent except Australia, New Zealand, and Antarctica?
Anemone: Genus of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Named for a mythological weaver transformed into a spider, which eight-legged class of arthropods includes scorpions, ticks, and mites?
Arachnid: Class of arthropods. The term is derived from the Greek word ἀράχνη (aráchnē, 'spider'), from the myth of the hubristic human weaver Arachne, who was turned into a spider.
This ocean giant, recorded at up to 680 kg, has vanished from the Black Sea but still roams the Mediterranean and both sides of another major ocean — which fish?
Atlantic bluefin tuna: Species of fish. The Atlantic bluefin tuna (Thunnus thynnus) is a species of tuna in the family Scombridae.

Developed in the 18th century by an English clergyman and, independently, by Pierre-Simon Laplace, this rule lets you flip a conditional probability — say, finding the odds a patient is sick given a positive test. What is it?
Bayes' theorem: Mathematical rule for inverting probabilities.
Prized for the rainbow, iridescent crust that forms when it oxidizes under heat, which brittle, silvery element is only 86 percent as dense as lead?
Bismuth: Chemical element with atomic number 83 (Bi)
Also nicknamed 'starflower,' this Mediterranean annual herb yields seed oil despite containing small amounts of toxic alkaloids — which plant?
Borage: Species of flowering plant in the family Boraginaceae.
One of the largest snake species on Earth, this Southeast Asian native became invasive in Florida after escaping the pet trade — which snake is this?
Burmese python: Species of large, nonvenomous snake.
Produced by chili peppers likely to deter hungry mammals, this hydrophobic compound is what gives them their burning, pungent kick — what is it?
Capsaicin: Pungent chemical compound in chili peppers. It is a potent irritant for mammals for which it produces a sensation of burning in any tissue with which it comes into contact.

This biological process splits a parent into two daughters, either producing genetically identical copies via mitosis or reducing chromosome number by half via meiosis to form gametes. What process is it?
Cell division: Biological process. Cell division usually occurs as part of a larger cell cycle in which the cell grows and replicates its chromosome(s) before dividing.
Known for a bitter metallic aftertaste that gets worse if you rinse with water, this antiseptic is used before surgery and to prevent dental plaque — what is it?
Chlorhexidine: Disinfectant and antiseptic. Chlorhexidine is a disinfectant and antiseptic which is used for skin disinfection before surgery and to disinfect surgical instruments.

First discovered as an atypical antipsychotic, this medication is reserved for schizophrenia patients who haven't responded to two other drugs, and is also used for psychosis linked to Parkinson's disease — what is it?
Clozapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Clozapine, sold under the brand name Clozaril among others, is a psychiatric medication and was the first atypical antipsychotic to be discovered.
These wind-pollinated, cone-bearing evergreens dominated Earth's landscapes throughout the Mesozoic before flowering plants took over — what group of plants is this?
Conifer: Group of seed plants. As of 2025, 94 conifer species are listed as endangered and 30 as critically endangered.
Their Latin name means 'those with shells,' and this mostly aquatic group includes crabs, lobsters, krill, barnacles, and mantis shrimp — what are they?
Named for a 19th-century British mathematician, this pair of logic rules shows how 'and' and 'or' swap places under negation — what are they called?
De Morgan's laws: Pair of logical equivalences.

Sudden lower-abdominal pain, sometimes a 'smoldering' slow burn over days — and the trouble is little abnormal pouches inflaming in the wall of your large intestine. What gastrointestinal disease is this?
Diverticulitis: Digestive disease of the large intestine. People may experience a single attack, repeated attacks, or ongoing "smoldering" diverticulitis.
Also known as dropsy, this medical condition involves fluid buildup in body tissue, often causing swelling in the legs or arms — what is it?
Edema: Accumulation of excess fluid in tissue.
This outermost skin layer ranges from about 31 micrometers thick on delicate areas to nearly 600 micrometers on the sole of the foot — what is it?
Epidermis: Outermost of the three layers that make up the skin.

One of the few birds known to pass the mirror test, this highly intelligent corvid found across the northern reaches of Eurasia has a nidopallium proportionally as large as a chimpanzee's brain — which bird is it?
Eurasian magpie: Species of bird. The Eurasian magpie or common magpie (Pica pica) is a resident breeding bird throughout the northern part of the Eurasian continent.

Named for the physicist who reportedly asked 'but where is everybody?' at Los Alamos in 1950, this puzzle questions why we've found no evidence of alien civilizations despite the odds favoring them — what's it called?
Fermi paradox: Discrepancy of the lack of evidence for alien life despite its apparent likelihood.
Called the "father of modern parasitology," this Italian physician-poet famously dismantled spontaneous generation by showing that maggots hatch from fly eggs — who was he?
Francesco Redi: Italian naturalist and poet. Francesco Redi (18 February 1626 – 1 March 1697) was an Italian physician, naturalist, biologist, and poet.
Once Mexico's top law-enforcement official as secretary of public security, this man was convicted in a Brooklyn courtroom in 2023 for taking millions in bribes from the Sinaloa Cartel — who is he?
Genaro García Luna: Mexican politician and convicted felon (born 1968)
Caused by iodine deficiency in over 90% of cases worldwide, this neck swelling results from an enlarged thyroid gland — what's the condition called?
Goitre: Neck swelling due to enlarged thyroid gland. A goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.

Named from Greek words meaning 'naked seed,' this group of woody plants — including conifers, cycads, and ginkgos — lacks the protective covering that encloses a flowering plant's seeds. What is it called?
Gymnosperm: Clade of non-flowering, naked-seeded vascular plants.
This Dutch-born entrepreneur produced Japan's first major turn-based role-playing game and later secured the console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game called Tetris — who is he?
Henk Rogers: Dutch-born American computer programmer (born 1953)
Despite the name, this 'living fossil' is no crustacean at all — it's a chelicerate, kin to spiders and scorpions, and its three-part body ends in a spiky tail called a telson. What creature is it?
Horseshoe crab: Family of basal chelicerates.
This mammal order today includes only small African and Middle Eastern hyraxes, but once boasted a species weighing up to 600 kilograms called Titanohyrax — which order?
Hyracoidea: Order of mammals. It includes the living hyraxes, placed within the family Procaviidae, and several extinct taxa.
She and her husband won the 1935 Nobel in Chemistry for discovering induced radioactivity — making her half of the only mother-daughter pair to both win Nobel Prizes. Who is this scientist?
Irène Joliot-Curie: French chemist and physicist (1897–1956)

This temporary condition throws your internal body clock out of sync with local time after rapid travel across multiple time zones — and most people find it harder to shake off flying east than west — what is it?

Jet lag: Condition due to travel across time zones. The phase shift when travelling from east to west is referred to as phase-delay of the circadian cycle, whereas going west to east is phase-advance of the cycle.

Known to NATO by the reporting name Hokum A and nicknamed 'Black Shark' for its distinctive coaxial rotors, this Russian single-seat attack helicopter has a rare rescue ejection system — which aircraft?
Kamov Ka-50: Attack helicopter. It was designed in the 1980s and adopted for service in the Russian army in 1995.
With a toothed, funnel-like sucking mouth, this jawless fish's name may derive from Latin for 'stone licker,' and it's genetically closer to hagfish than to any jawed vertebrate — what is it?
Lamprey: Class of jawless fish. Lampreys (sometimes inaccurately called lamprey eels) are a group of jawless fish composing the order Petromyzontiformes, sole order in the class Petromyzontida.
This genus of bulb-grown flowering plants, prized for their large blooms, is highly toxic to cats — even though many unrelated plants borrow its common name — which genus?
Lilium: Genus of plants. Lilium ( LIL-ee-əm) is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants growing from bulbs, all with large and often prominent flowers.
Originating in 1993 and written in ANSI C, this lightweight scripting language was designed to be embedded inside other applications — which language?
Lua: Lightweight programming language. Lua is a lightweight, high-level, multi-paradigm programming language designed mainly for embedded use in applications.
Sharing joints only with the temporal bones, this is the skull's lone movable bone, hosting the lower teeth and shrinking in size since humans began farming around 10,000 BCE — what is it called?
Mandible: Lower jaw bone. The mandible hosts the lower teeth (their depth delineated by the alveolar process).
Its name means 'big tooth,' and this extinct giant mackerel shark — once mistaken for a great white relative — is known only from fragmentary remains. What is it?
Megalodon: Extinct giant shark species. Megalodon probably had a major impact on the structure of marine communities.

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
Known as simple sugars, these colorless, water-soluble crystalline compounds include glucose and fructose and serve as the building blocks of starch and cellulose — what are they called?
Monosaccharide: Simple sugars such as glucose and fructose.

This inner-ear condition brings on episodes of vertigo, ringing in the ears, and hearing loss lasting anywhere from 20 minutes to several hours — believed to stem from fluid buildup in the labyrinth. What is it?
Ménière's disease: Disorder of the inner ear. The hearing loss and ringing in the ears can become constant over time.
Its name literally means 'blue cow,' though only the males actually sport a bluish-grey coat — which is the largest antelope species in Asia?

The type species that gives its name to the Oleaceae family of lilac, jasmine, and ash, this Mediterranean evergreen bears a fruit classed botanically as a drupe — like a cherry or peach — what is it?
Also known as jícama or Mexican turnip, this pea-family vine's edible tuberous root comes in a milky-juice form and a watery-juice form — which species is it?
Pachyrhizus erosus: Species of legume. Pachyrhizus tuberosus and Pachyrhizus ahipa are the other two cultivated species in the genus.
Often described simply as the act of teaching, this discipline studies how knowledge and skills are imparted — and how that process shapes learners socially and psychologically. What is it?
Pedagogy: Theory and practice of education.
This branch of linguistics studies how speech sounds are articulated, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived, split into three sub-disciplines — what field is it?
Phonetics: Study of how humans produce and perceive sounds.
Home to cereal crops like wheat, rice, and maize as well as bamboo, this is the fifth-largest plant family on Earth — what is it called?
Poaceae: Family of flowering plants commonly known as grasses.
This beta blocker treats high blood pressure and performance anxiety alike, and can even shrink capillary hemangiomas in infants — what drug?
Propranolol: Beta blocker drug. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.
First identified in the 1950s as a radio source, this extremely luminous galactic nucleus can outshine an entire galaxy like the Milky Way thousands of times over — what is it?
Quasar: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) containing a supermassive black hole.
Often compared to the film in a camera, this innermost, light-sensitive layer of the eye sends signals along the optic nerve to the visual cortex — what is it?
Retina: Part of the eye. The retina (from Latin rete 'net'; pl. retinae or retinas) is the innermost, light-sensitive layer of tissue of the eye.
